candidate.title: SHAPE-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned SHAPE-Seq middle row: in vitro barcoded RNA, 1M7 probing, two example modification-dependent reverse-transcription outcomes, and RNA hydrolysis to cDNA. The card title and the matching page-78 heading/caption identify this target. ICE and icSHAPE are separately labeled neighboring rows in the supplied crop, not alternatives of SHAPE-Seq. The left highlighted hairpin expands the method name and is not an additional routed operation. The supplied abstract supports sequencing of primer-extension products; adapter installation, amplification, sequencing, controls and analysis are not drawn and are not reconstructed as operations. The depicted cDNA population represents RNA structural reactivity through extension endpoints and RNA identity through the barcode association, rather than directly sequencing the modified RNA. The library boundary is the isolated primer-extension cDNA, not a claimed fully specified sequencing-ready library. Chemical reactivity and extension endpoints provide structural constraints; background reverse-transcriptase drop-off prevents interpreting every endpoint as an adduct without the controls described by the catalogue.

operations.label: 1M7 reaction

The upper and lower RT and hydrolysis instances preserve the separate drawn outcomes under shared captions. They illustrate different mark positions, not treated versus untreated samples or separately named assays. The page-78 heading and A schematic overview of SHAPE-Seq caption match the target and describe the barcode/folding/1M7 order. Lucks et al. is associated by the poster fragment, complete catalogue reference and supplied PubMed identity; only its abstract content was inspected. Neither the in-cell SHAPE-Seq application nor the adjacent icSHAPE row is included. The catalogue also lists a Watters, Yu, Strobel, Settle and Lucks Methods (2016) protocol as reference 150; only that secondary citation was inspected, no primary record for it is supplied, and it is not used to support additional operations or expand the method scope.
